name: Map Chunk Bulk
desc: Sends multiple chunks at once. Used for initial world load and large area updates.

fields.name: chunks
fields.desc: Array of chunk data with X/Z/bitmask/compressed data

encoding: X, Z, bitmask, dataSize, compressed data
notes: S26 is the bulk version of S21 — sends many chunks in a single packet. Used on world join and loading large areas. XRay modules also cancel S26 alongside S21 to prevent chunk updates.

writeup.p: S26 is the bulk chunk loader: one packet carrying many chunk columns with a shared sky-light flag. Each column is x/z ints, a 16-bit section bitmask, a VarInt data size, then the compressed section data. The server builds it in EntityPlayerMP when a player joins or moves between chunk groups (corpus line 330), batching all newly-loaded columns so the client can decode them in one pass. It is the load-bearing packet for world join and teleport.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleMapChunkBulk loops the columns, calls doPreChunk to mark each as loaded, invalidates the block receive region, then reads each chunk via the shared PacketUtil.readCompressed path and loads it into the world. Sky-light presence is decided once per packet by the boolean flag. The client then re-renders the whole batch; on 1.8.9 this is one of the few handlers that visibly blocks the render thread while decompressing.

Zero module hits in the 8-client corpus. The only non-vanilla reference is Rise 6.x's script NetworkAPI class registration. The packet metadata for S26 mentions XRay cancelling bulk chunks, but in these 8 clients no XRay module references S26PacketMapChunkBulk at all (Tenacity's XRay touches S21PacketChunkData, not S26). The absence is practical: cancelling S26 on a join breaks the world wholesale, and the ores an XRay wants to hide are already filtered in the chunk-render path, not at the packet layer.

The real abuse surface is server-to-client: a malicious server can send an S26 with an enormous uncompressed payload or a huge column count to stall the client's decompression loop, a classic 1.8 lag-machine vector. Client-side there is nothing to exploit; the packet is inbound truth. Chunk-banning clients that want to blank specific regions do it by editing the column bitmask before the vanilla handler runs, which no module in this corpus implements for S26.

implementation.overview: The bulk chunk-load packet used on join and teleport. Zero modules in the 8 clients consume it; the only non-vanilla reference is Rise 6.x's scripting API registration. Its payload is inbound world truth, and the exploitable direction is server to client.
implementation.server_handling: EntityPlayerMP gathers pending ChunkCoordIntPair columns and constructs S26 when the load queue is flushed. The sky-light boolean is set once from the world's dimension provider. There is no per-packet size cap in vanilla; the server trusts its own chunk generation. A client can request chunks (C03 position movement) but cannot dictate the bulk layout.
implementation.protocol_notes: Wire format: boolean skyLightSent, VarInt column count, then per column: int x, int z, short bitmask, VarInt data length, compressed byte[]. The bitmask is a 16-bit section selector; sections absent from the mask are inherited from the previous chunk state. The compressed payload is zlib via PacketUtil.readCompressed, with the data length prefix on the wire.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat inspects S26 content; it is inbound and unspoofable. The relevant protection is on the client: crash-patch modules that bound the column count or payload size. None of the 8 clients ship one for S26 specifically; Tenacity's AntiExploit covers explosion and particle floods instead.
implementation.general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent on all clients; no module registers for S26 in the corpus.
implementation.client_variations: All 8 clients keep the vanilla handler. Rise 6.1.30/6.2.4 expose S26 in the script NetworkAPI table only. Tenacity's XRay/Search chunk filtering is done against S21PacketChunkData, not S26.

anticheat.overview: S26 is the bulk chunk variant of S21 used by 1.7 and 1.8 servers: one packet carries several chunk columns with a shared skylight flag. Anticheats treat it exactly like the single-chunk packet: the bytes are decoded into the compensated world (Grim PacketWorldReaderEight handleMapChunkBulk, Intave MapChunkBulkReader, Kauri World update via ChunkDataBulk, Truthful CompensatedWorld via the global chunk cache), and the same xray and world-downloader protections apply (Photon WorldDownloaderSentinel). The corpus for S26 is therefore the replication pipeline with bulk-specific readers.

checks.name: PacketWorldReaderEight map-chunk-bulk (Grim)
checks.purpose: Decode the S26 bulk packet into Grim's compensated world, column by column.
checks.how_it_works: handleMapChunkBulk reads the skylight boolean, column count, and per-column x/z and section masks, then for each column decodes the 16 sections with the 1.8 palette reader, skips the 256 biome bytes plus 2048 block-light (and 2048 sky-light when the flag is set) per section, and merges the column into the compensated world cache with the transaction id. The dispatch lives in BasePacketWorldReader, which routes chunk-data-bulk packets here.
checks.detects: Feeds the ground, collision and phase simulation the same way handleMapChunk does for S21; bulk loading cannot bypass the cache.
checks.variations: Intave MapChunkBulkReader reads only the per-column x/z coordinate arrays and hands them to the block cache; Kauri runUpdate(WrapperPlayServerChunkDataBulk) applies bulk columns inside keepalive actions; Hydro WorldTracker handleChunkBulk stores the sections in its chunk map.

checks.name: MapChunkBulkReader (Intave)
checks.purpose: Read the chunk coordinates of every column in the S26 bulk packet for Intave's chunk coordinate tracking.
checks.how_it_works: ChunkCoordinateReader implementation that clones the packet's x and z integer arrays, giving the block cache the coordinates of every column in the bulk; PacketReaders registers it as setup(MAP_CHUNK_BULK, MapChunkBulkReader::new). The coordinates feed the multi-chunk block cache that physics and interaction checks use.
checks.detects: Keeps the block cache's chunk grid in sync when whole regions load at once; no direct flag.
checks.variations: Grim handleMapChunkBulk and Kauri runUpdate(WrapperPlayServerChunkDataBulk) decode the full columns; ChunkCoordinateReader is Intave's shared interface with MapChunkReader for S21.

checks.name: WorldDownloaderSentinel (Photon)
checks.purpose: Detect WorldDownloader mods at the wdl channel handshake and disable their chunk caching and saving.
checks.how_it_works: Same module as the S21 entry: it answers wdl|INIT with wdl|CONTROL packets that disable general saving, chunk caching, entity, tile-entity and container saving per config, then runs the sentinel detection. Bulk chunk delivery (S26) is the mod's highest-bandwidth input, so the module closes the hole before the client can persist anything.
checks.detects: WorldDownloader clients on 1.7 and 1.8 servers, where the bulk packet makes whole-region capture trivial.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus speaks the wdl channels; Negativity and LightAntiCheat approximate the protection with region bypass and unloaded-chunk checks.

checks.name: Chunk column cache (Kauri)
checks.purpose: Store the 16x384x16 block grid of each replicated chunk so Kauri's checks can query block states.
checks.how_it_works: Chunk holds a synchronized WrappedBlock[16][384][16] array keyed by chunk x/z; updateBlock writes into it (with the negative-y offset for 1.18 worlds) and getBlockAt returns an Optional of the block, mapping coordinates into the local grid. World fills these chunks from chunk-data and chunk-data-bulk packets via runUpdate, and BlockUpdateHandler routes S22 and S23 updates into the same storage.
checks.detects: Supplies block truth for Kauri's phase, reach and interaction checks; the S26 corpus hit is the ChunkDataBulk consumption in BlockUpdateHandler that fills these grids.
checks.variations: Truthful CompensatedWorld delegates to a global world cache of ChunkSnapshot objects with a last-chunk access cache; Hydro WorldTracker stores PacketEvents BaseChunk arrays; Grim Column records hold BaseChunk[] plus the transaction id.
